answer: One defense is graph-based trust: every agent builds a history of reciprocal exchanges, like a river fed by many small streams. A Sybil cluster forms a closed loop, its members trading only with each other, so their interaction graph looks like a stagnant pond while honest agents connect broadly across the network. Newcomers start on a low terrace of trust and gain access gradually as their links diversify, so an attacker who must fake thousands of genuine cross-cutting relationships faces a cost that rises with every tide of fake identities, making large-scale forgery uneconomical.
